overview.title: Platform Overview
overview.intro: Understand the platform layout and learning path
overview.s0: This is a pure front-end poker training tool that requires no registration. Courses, focused drills, quick reviews, hand-history analysis and progress tracking all run in your browser. Your learning data is never uploaded to a server.

s1-steps.0: Open /lesson to see your next lesson, theory chapters and due reviews
s1-steps.1: Take the placement assessment and switch between standard, heads-up and short-deck variants in the Course Hub
s1-steps.2: Choose a focused range, pot-odds, GTO or puzzle session
s1-steps.3: Review progress and weaknesses, then return to a lesson or quick drill to reinforce them

overview.s2: Tip: You do not need to follow a fixed order. Address weaknesses first, use short sessions to stay sharp, and favor consistent practice over occasional marathons.

range-trainer.title: Range Trainer
range-trainer.intro: Learn and quiz starting-hand ranges by position and variant
range-trainer.s0: Range Trainer uses 13×13 matrices, a short-deck matrix and position presets to build your position–action–hand intuition. Learn mode is for exploration; Quiz mode checks your recall.

s1-steps.0: Choose standard, heads-up or short-deck; standard mode also supports table-size presets
s1-steps.1: Select a position and action preset, then browse the range in Learn mode
s1-steps.2: Enter Quiz mode and correct frequently missed positions from instant feedback
s1-steps.3: Watch unlock hints; wider positions open gradually as the relevant ELO progresses

range-trainer.s2: Common mistake: Do not memorize colors alone. Understand why position and action matter first. A range is a thinking framework, not a fixed answer for every hand.

pot-odds.title: Pot Odds Calculator
pot-odds.intro: Master pot odds, draw estimates and EV calculations
pot-odds.s0: The calculator estimates required calling equity from the pot, opponent bet and outs, with an equity chart and draw reference. The EV tab compares costs, payoffs and probability assumptions, but it does not replace reading the hand.

s1-steps.0: Enter the current pot size and opponent's bet
s1-steps.1: Estimate your outs and compare required equity with estimated equity
s1-steps.2: Switch to the EV tab to inspect payoff, cost and probability assumptions
s1-steps.3: Take the timed quiz to build speed and boundary judgment

pot-odds.s2: Common mistake: Do not double-count outs when flush and straight draws overlap. Estimated equity is not live equity; opponent ranges and future action still change the result.

gto-simulator.title: GTO Simulator
gto-simulator.intro: Practice GTO decisions in pre-computed scenarios
gto-simulator.s0: The GTO Simulator offers pre-computed preflop, flop, turn and river scenarios. After you act, it compares your choice with the scenario's optimal action and explains the EV loss.

s1-steps.0: Configure a session or open single-spot training
s1-steps.1: Read the position, board and action history, then fold, call or raise
s1-steps.2: Review the optimal action, EV loss and explanation
s1-steps.3: Open the result summary and revisit related lessons

gto-simulator.s2: Common mistake: GTO is a baseline, not the only live answer. Exploitative adjustments can be better against readable tendencies; understand the cost of deviating before adjusting.

academy.title: Strategy Academy & Course Hub
academy.intro: Course path, practical map, 8-level curriculum and certification
academy.s0: The Course Hub at /lesson is the shared entry for standard, heads-up and short-deck variants. It shows the next lesson, theory chapters, mastery and reviews. The practical map at /academy shows the strategy ladder, placement, checkpoints and study tools.

s1-steps.0: Start with the next action in the Course Hub and complete lessons and drills by stage
s1-steps.1: Switch variants in the Course Hub; L1/L2 share foundations while L3–L8 use variant-specific content
s1-steps.2: Use the practical map for levels, theory bridges, placement and checkpoints
s1-steps.3: After completing a standard-variant level, take its certification at 70% accuracy

academy.s2: Certification is standard-variant only: it lasts 30 days, with a 24-hour cooldown after a failed attempt. Heads-up and short-deck currently do not offer level certification.

theory.title: Theory Academy
theory.intro: The T1–T9 theory system, chapter quizzes and practice bridges
theory.s0: Theory Academy at /theory is the theory map. It presents T1–T9 core chapters for the active variant, covering probability, EV, position, ranges, GTO, betting, hand reading, psychology and integrated frameworks, with bridges into strategy lessons.

s1-steps.0: Choose a core chapter from the current level on the theory map
s1-steps.1: Finish the reading and quiz; completing core chapters advances the level
s1-steps.2: Use search, glossary, bookmarks and flagged-question review to find content
s1-steps.3: Follow practice bridges to the related strategy lesson or trainer

theory.s2: Supplemental chapters are optional reinforcement and do not gate levels or core progress. Placement can grant credit, but credited chapters are not marked completed.

quick-drill.title: Quick Drill
quick-drill.intro: Weakness focus, SRS review and adaptive difficulty
quick-drill.s0: Quick Drill at /quick combines learned lessons, recent weaknesses and due reviews into short sessions. Default quick mode uses 5 questions and adapts difficulty from standard-variant ELO; regular practice mode uses 8 questions.

s1-steps.0: Choose preflop, math or mixed mode; quick mode keeps focus within the matching weakness dimension
s1-steps.1: Start the session; the system prioritizes weak lessons and mixes in due reviews
s1-steps.2: Review your score, best record and quick-drill streak after finishing
s1-steps.3: Complete quick drills on 7 consecutive days to earn 1 freeze card

quick-drill.s2: Quick Drill maintains familiarity but does not replace a full lesson. If consecutive mistakes trigger a difficulty drop, review the explanations and basics before increasing speed.

puzzle.title: Poker Puzzles
puzzle.intro: Daily puzzles, timed rush and topic drills
puzzle.s0: Puzzle Trainer offers three local modes: a Daily Puzzle with 8 fixed questions seeded by the local date, a 3- or 5-minute Rush, and topic drills for themes such as RFI and 3-bet.

s1-steps.0: Daily Puzzle: finish today's fixed set and review explanations and your local best score
s1-steps.1: Rush: choose 3 or 5 minutes and balance speed with accuracy
s1-steps.2: Topic Drill: focus on one weak decision category
s1-steps.3: Review your answer streak and revisit related lessons

puzzle.s2: Daily Puzzle is offline and has no real global ranking. The companion count is a local demo, not a live player count. Understand each decision before chasing speed.

hand-history.title: Hand History
hand-history.intro: Import, replay, annotate and review rule-based deviations
hand-history.s0: Hand History imports .txt histories from PokerStars, GGPoker and PartyPoker. It locally parses seats, actions, community cards and pots, then provides replay, annotations and a rule-based GTO deviation reference.

s1-steps.0: Export hand-history text from your poker platform
s1-steps.1: Paste or upload the .txt file and choose the matching platform format
s1-steps.2: Open a hand, replay actions street by street and add annotations
s1-steps.3: Review deviation references; a stats summary appears after at least 20 hands

hand-history.s2: The deviation panel is a local rule-based reference, not exact node-by-node solver analysis. Remove player identifiers you do not want stored in your local environment before importing.

progress.title: Progress Tracking
progress.intro: Track ELO, streaks, accuracy and weaknesses
progress.s0: Progress aggregates training records across modules, showing five-dimension ELO, streaks, accuracy trends, weakness analysis and due reviews. Standard, heads-up and short-deck ELO are tracked separately.

s1-steps.0: Review today's volume, ELO changes and streak on the dashboard
s1-steps.1: Open detailed stats to compare modules and variants
s1-steps.2: Use weakness analysis and due reviews to choose the next session
s1-steps.3: Return to the Course Hub to check mastery and unfinished chapters

progress.s2: ELO reflects training performance, not real-world win rate. Small samples fluctuate more; judge progress alongside accuracy, difficulty and hand-history review.

settings.title: Settings & Data Management
settings.intro: Appearance, language, training preferences, backups and developer options
settings.s0: Settings controls appearance, language, mentor style, sound, timing, question counts, daily limits, game variant and freeze cards. It also provides data export, import and developer options.

s1-steps.0: Adjust default time, question count and daily cap to match your goal
s1-steps.1: Export a JSON backup on the old device before switching devices
s1-steps.2: Import it on the new device; records are validated and duplicates are skipped
s1-steps.3: Hand histories migrate with a complete backup; read failures are clearly marked as partial

settings.s2: Clear Training Records removes training history only. ELO, review queue, settings, academy progress and hand histories remain. Clearing browser site data removes local content and cannot be undone.

concepts.title: System Concepts
concepts.subtitle: Brief explanations of the six core systems

elo.title: ELO Rating System
elo.body: ELO rates preflop, postflop, math, hand reading and mental dimensions separately for standard, heads-up and short-deck. Overall is the five-dimension average. Correctness and difficulty affect each change, across 6 ranks.

streak.title: Streak & Freeze Cards
streak.body: Training records consecutive days. Milestones at 3/7/30/100/365 days award 1/2/3/5/10 freeze cards. Missing one day starts a free 24-hour recovery window; you can also manually protect today from Settings.

srs.title: SRS Spaced Repetition
srs.body: A simplified SM-2 scheduler advances or shortens review intervals from your answers. Due items appear in the Course Hub and Quick Drill; a mistake does not force immediate repetition, but schedules another review.

feedback.title: Five-Level Feedback
feedback.body: Where EV loss is calibrated, feedback uses best, correct, inaccuracy, wrong and blunder. Content without EV semantics, such as theory chapter quizzes, keeps binary correctness instead of showing an artificial five-level badge.

sessionLimit.title: Daily Question Limit
sessionLimit.body: Settings offers 0, 50, 100 or 200 questions. Reaching the cap prevents a new session from starting but does not interrupt one in progress. Debug unlock can temporarily bypass it.

dataStorage.title: Data Storage & Export
dataStorage.body: Settings and learning state use localStorage; training records and hand histories use IndexedDB. A complete JSON backup includes records, settings and readable hand data. Clearing browser site data removes local content.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Common questions about data, language, offline, freeze cards

q0.question: Where is my data stored?
q0.answer: Settings and state such as ELO and streaks use localStorage, while training records and hand histories use IndexedDB. Nothing is uploaded to a server. Clearing browser site data or switching browsers causes data loss, so export backups regularly.

q1.question: How do I migrate data to a new device?
q1.answer: Export Data in Settings downloads a JSON backup. Import Data on the new device validates and merges records, skips duplicates, and restores supported settings and hand histories. If hands cannot be read, the app clearly marks the backup as partial.

q2.question: Does it work offline?
q2.answer: Yes. After the first successful load and Service Worker pre-cache, cached pages and resources work offline. Offline mode does not sync data; moving to another device still requires a JSON backup.

q3.question: How do I switch languages?
q3.answer: Use the language button in the top bar or sidebar, or the language dropdown in Settings. Changes apply immediately and the preference is saved automatically.

q4.question: How do I get and use freeze cards?
q4.answer: Streaks of 3/7/30/100/365 days award 1/2/3/5/10 cards. Before training today, you may manually use one card in Settings while the streak is still recoverable. It is unavailable after training today, after daily use, without cards, or outside the recovery window. The 24-hour Earn Back recovery after one missed day is free.

q5.question: What happens if my streak breaks?
q5.answer: After one missed day, your next training within the 24-hour window restores the previous streak for free. After the window expires, the count restarts at 1. ELO is unaffected; begin with basics to rebuild momentum.

q6.question: What is debug unlock?
q6.answer: Debug unlock in Developer Options bypasses course levels, local-lesson nodes, theory chapter deep links, range positions, learning-track prerequisites and daily question limits for development testing. Regular users do not need it, and it does not alter existing learning data.

q7.question: Can I recover data after clearing?
q7.answer: Clear Training Records removes training history only and keeps ELO, reviews, settings, academy progress and hand histories; it cannot be undone. Clearing browser site data removes local learning content, which can only be restored from a previously exported JSON backup.

q8.question: Does Daily Puzzle connect online or create a global ranking?
q8.answer: No. Daily Puzzle seeds 8 fixed questions from the built-in bank using the local date. There is no account, server leaderboard or data upload. The companion count is a local demo, not a live player count.

q9.question: How do I switch between standard, heads-up and short-deck?
q9.answer: The Course Hub at /lesson is the unified variant switch for strategy and theory. Ladders, chapters and mastery follow the selected variant, and ELO is tracked separately for each one.

q10.question: How long is Strategy Academy certification valid?
q10.answer: Certification is standard-variant only. A score of 70% passes, and the certificate remains valid for 30 days. A failed attempt has a 24-hour cooldown; expired certification can be retaken.
